text:
Maria: Heads up — eu-west GPU pool is saturated, large number of Pending pods requesting nvidia-gpu. Alerting shows cluster-autoscaler repeatedly trying to scale. Noticed at ~08:05 UTC.
Devon: I'm on the dashboards. Autoscaler logs show scale-up then immediate provisioning failures, lots of ENI/attach errors.
Maria: Can someone dump pending pods and owners?
Devon: Pasting `kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide | grep gpu` output:
```
research   sweep-ctrl-1845-0        0/1  Pending  0   3m  
research   sweep-worker-xx         0/1  Pending  0   4m  
research   sweep-worker-yy         0/1  Pending  0   2m  
inference  rerank-2026-03-18-a    0/1  Pending  0   1m  
```
Maria: Looks like Research job controller spawned a bunch of sweep workers after a schedule change. That explains the sudden demand.
Ryan: Cluster-autoscaler tail (abridged):
```
I0318 08:06:12 autoscaler.go:234] Scale-up: want 10 nodes, have 2, cores/GPUs needed
I0318 08:06:40 azureprovider.go:120] AttachNetworkInterface failed: no available IPs in subnet
I0318 08:07:05 autoscaler.go:401] Backoff 5m: recent failures preventing further scale-ups
```
Alex: So root cause = subnet IP exhaustion (ENI limit). Cloud quotas show vNICs nearly saturated in eu-west.
Maria: Immediate mitigation proposals: 1) pause new research sweeps, 2) aggressively cordon the research nodepool to stop autoscaler from targeting it, 3) evict low-priority jobs, 4) move critical inference to fallback pool/region.
Devon: Implementing step 1: hitting research API to pause new runs.
```
$ curl -s -X POST https://research-api.internal/api/v1/sweeps/pause -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"reason":"emergency pause"}'
{"status":"ok","paused_inflight":86}
```
Alex: Step 2: disabled autoscaling on pool `research-gpu-eu` and cordoned nodes.
```
$ gcloud container node-pools update research-gpu-eu --cluster=prod-eu --disable-autoscaling
$ kubectl cordon -l pool=research-eu
$ kubectl taint nodes -l pool=research-eu gpu-spill=true:NoSchedule
```
Ryan: After cordon, cluster-autoscaler stopped considering those pending pods for scale-up. Also opened cloud support ticket (CASE# CL-91234) to request ENI/vNIC quota increase for eu-west — ETA several hours.
Maria: While quota is pending, we need to free GPUs quickly. Suggest evicting non-prod pods with low priority-class and draining test pools.
Devon: Executed eviction for preemptible/test pools using `priorityClass=low-test` and `--grace-period=20`. Freed ~8 GPUs. Also patched sweep controller deployment to gate concurrency to 10.
```
$ kubectl patch deployment sweep-controller -n research --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"controller","env":[{"name":"MAX_SWEEPS","value":"10"}]}]}}}}'
```
Alex: Good. Also set autoscaler max surge to limit excessive simultaneous node requests (temporary).
Devon: Updated cluster-autoscaler flags to `--max-node-provisioning-rate=2` to slow down bursts and avoid repeated ENI attempts.
Maria: Monitoring: GPU usage in eu-west dropped from ~99% -> ~58% across 10 minutes. Pending count reduced as controller paused new launches. Autoscaler backoff cleared and stabilised.
Ryan: For a mid-term fix: propose adding ENI/Quota checks into our provisioning pipeline and an autoscaler backoff heuristic on ENI errors. I'll own the quota-sensing PR.
Alex: Action items: rollback the scheduler change that introduced the bug (assigned Alex), add global rate-limit to sweep API (assigned Maria), autoscaler guard for ENI attach failures (assigned Devon), and provisioning quota-awareness (assigned Ryan).
ops-bot: Incident resolved (08:32 UTC) — service degraded -> recovered. Runbook executed: gpu-eni-exhaustion-v1. Please file incident report: /incidents/2467890123.
Maria: Thanks everyone — nice rapid coordination. We'll follow up in the postmortem and add a test to simulate ENI exhaustion during scale-up. :thumbsup:
